study.question: Does protecting the two greatest-index fully occupied history blocks preserve more click-predictive summary information than protecting the two endpoints or two least-index blocks, when the number of protected/movable blocks, parameter capacity, training exposure and RNG draws are matched?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: g2-r0087-summary_newest_anchor reaches click AUC0.6678289796, above oldest-only0.6664307105 and unrestricted0.6655000295, but below supplied0.6689612706. Provisional mechanism: some remaining useful summary information is localized to the next-greatest-index full block, rather than explained entirely by one endpoint or by the number of blocks spared from permutation. Preserving the two greatest-index full-block locations should improve over newest-only and over an equal-count endpoint pair; the two-oldest control probes opposite-end symmetry. This predicts location-specific utility of intact block assignments under this architecture, not pairwise temporal-transition utility, real-time recency or a new architecture.

study.proposed_difference: Implement six complete-event block maps in all cells and select one of newest_two, endpoints, oldest_two or newest. A full block has all10 valid positions. For ordered full-block IDs F, protected sets are last2(F), {first(F),last(F)}, first2(F), or last1(F), respectively, with set semantics for small F. Uniformly permute only other full blocks with shared random priorities; leave their local offsets and all nonfull slots fixed. The first three have min(2,|F|) anchors and identical eligible counts. There is no new learned representation or claimed novelty.
predictions: Predeclared primary contrast: full-population validation click AUC(newest_two)-AUC(endpoints)>0.0001, with matched host conditions and effective perturbations. This is a prospective practical screening margin, not a significance threshold or guaranteed effect.

Corroborating contrasts: newest_two exceeds oldest_two and the newest-only bridge. Recovery toward supplied0.6689612706 indicates where summary-order utility resides; no requirement to beat the supplied incumbent.

If location matters, the strongest direct input-treatment differences are in rows with >=4 full blocks; for <=3 full blocks every two-anchor map is identity. Predictions after retraining need not coincide on untreated rows because parameters are shared.

Expected parameter count remains32192421 total/31793216 embedding/399205 dense, subject to host measurement. Runtime should remain near prior450-473s units plus extra map construction; measure rather than assume cost equality.
Newest-only bridge reproduces g2-r0087-summary_newest_anchor at the frozen seed; same input maps, RNG advancement, state keys and learned arithmetic should match before interpreting new arms.
falsifiers: Effective matched treatments with newest_two no better than endpoints or oldest_two fail the location-specific hypothesis for this implementation; equal improvement of all pair treatments over newest-only instead favors reduced perturbation.

If newest_two fails to improve over a valid newest-only bridge, there is no support here that preserving the next block contributes additional predictive utility; a failed implementation is not a general refutation of order utility.

Bridge mismatch, event/membership corruption, changed mask/target, ineffective order alteration, nonfinite outputs/gradients, unexpected parameter changes or failing inherited VJP checks invalidate interpretation and require a charged correction, not a scientific positive or null.
